**Summary of evidence:**

- **Anthracnose** (pod/seed): Dark black lesions on fruit — clearly a fruit disease, not matching the leaf symptoms in the test image. **Ruled out.**
- **Cigar_End_Rot** (pod): Tip rot on banana fingers — fruit disease. **Ruled out.**
- **Cordana_Leaf_Spot**: Discrete dark brown oval spots with yellow halos on green leaves — no spots visible in test image. **Ruled out.**
- **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka**: Yellow patches with distinct dark brown/black necrotic lesions — no discrete lesions in test image. **Ruled out.**
- **Bunchy_Top**: Stunted compact plant, leaves clustered at top, dark green vein streaks. Some visual similarity in bunching, but no characteristic dark green streaks visible; leaves appear full-sized in test image. **Less likely.**
- **Panama_Disease**: Diffuse yellowing starting at leaf margins/base, graduating to green toward the blade center/tip. The `Banana_Leaf_1043.jpg` reference showing yellow margin banding on an otherwise green leaf is the closest visual match to the test image — same gradient pattern from yellow at base/margin to green at the leaf blade center.

The test image shows banana leaves with **diffuse basal/marginal yellowing** (yellow-green at base transitioning to green), no discrete spots or streaks, and overlapping/wilted leaf positioning — consistent with the early-to-mid stages of Panama Disease (Fusarium wilt).
